questions.q: Why does this report use a bar chart rather than a pie chart, even though there are only four categories?
options: A pie chart would not fit on the same page as the KPI cards
Bar charts are required whenever there are fewer than ten categories
Bar length is easier to compare precisely than wedge angle, and bars can be sorted to show a clear ranking, which a pricing review needs
Pie charts cannot be built in Power BI
questions.explain: Even with a small number of slices, angle comparisons are less precise than length comparisons, and bars can be sorted highest-to-lowest -- something a pie chart has no equivalent for.

questions.q: Why does this layout use a flat table instead of a matrix for the detail visual?
options: There is only one grouping dimension (category), so there is nothing to pivot rows against columns
A table always loads faster than a matrix regardless of the data
The T-SQL query returns data in a format matrices cannot read
Matrices are not available in Power BI Desktop
questions.explain: A matrix earns its place when pivoting two dimensions against each other; with just one grouping dimension here, a flat table is the simpler, correct fit.

questions.q: Why does this report's layout skip a line chart entirely?
options: Line charts require at least five categories
Line charts cannot display currency-formatted values
The KPI cards already replace the need for any chart
There is only one quarter of data, so there is no trend over time to show
questions.explain: A line chart is built to show change over time; with a single quarter's worth of data, there's no time series for it to meaningfully display.

questions.q: What do the two KPI cards answer, according to this lesson?
options: Which specific category had the highest sales
"How are we doing, overall" -- in the first half-second of looking at the page
The exact order count for each individual category
Whether the quarter-over-quarter trend is positive or negative
questions.explain: The KPI cards are the company-wide totals, meant to answer the overall question at a glance before any more detailed visual is read.

questions.q: What is the main point of sketching the report layout before opening the Visualizations pane?
options: Power BI requires a saved sketch file before visuals can be added
It is only useful for reports with more than three visuals
It avoids a report that looks assembled rather than designed, with visuals placed based on what question they need to answer
It eliminates the need to pick a visual type later
questions.explain: The same discipline as planning the query in plain English first: deciding what each visual needs to answer before dragging anything onto the canvas.
